rationale: Two attempts observed: attempt-00 (block_M=128,block_N=64,block_K=64,stages=1,threads=256,swizzle=0) simulated 157.29us at smem=32768, 2 blocks/SM; attempt-01 (block_M=32,block_N=128,block_K=32,stages=3,threads=256,swizzle=16) was slower at 186.64us despite more blocks/SM (3) and lower registers, indicating the smaller block_M/block_K and deeper pipeline did not pay off - likely extra launch/tile count and swizzle panel not helping with this geometry. Both compiled, passed numerics/SMT. Since M=128 a single block_M=128 tile row gives no panel reuse benefit, so keep block_M domain broad including 64/128 to allow multi-row alternatives, but retain 16/32 only for parallelism probes. Keep block_N up to 256 to test wider N tiles that cut launches. Block_K includes 128 to probe longer per-stage work with fewer stages; stages limited to 2-4 because stage=1 underperformed vs stage=3 in attempt-01 pattern (though 00 was fastest). Threads kept 128/256 (64 unmeasured, 256 worked; 128 to test warp layout sensitivity). Swizzle now expanded to all allowed values [0,4,8,16,32,64] per post-baseline instruction, but full-sweep of swizzle alone is discouraged since M has few tile rows when block_M=128; combine with block_K=128 and stages=4 as the next hypothesis. Weights: reduce footprint to 0.75 (smem already at cap and not the bottleneck), raise pipeline to 1.5 to favor deeper overlap at block_K=64/128, keep traffic/launches at 1. Shared limit stays 32768 (hard portability cap). Next hypothesis: block_M=64/128 with block_N=128/256, block_K=128, stages=3-4, threads=128/256, testing whether larger tiles with deeper K-pipelining recover or beat the 157.29us baseline; validation scope note: Metal executed exact source/config/TIR numerics, CUDA binary not executed, GB10 latencies are simulator estimates only, not hardware measurements.
